propositions: The Reconcile Bridge ran on GitHub Actions and produced zero CloudWatch signal when the Jira API token expired, leaving the failure invisible to monitoring systems that only poll the host.
GitHub Actions can publish CloudWatch metrics via OIDC federation but the repo did not yet implement this pattern for the bridge.
The bridge failure notification existed only as a workflow step summary and GitHub annotation, visible only to those already viewing the run.

Publishing a 0 metric on successful bridge runs ensures the publisher itself remains continuously observable and distinguishable from a broken or unauthorized publisher, rather than relying on missing-data semantics that would leave the alarm in INSUFFICIENT_DATA during healthy periods.
A new IAM role narrowly scoped to cloudwatch:PutMetricData with namespace condition rebar/host was required to federate the workflow without widening existing roles or granting broad permissions.

The CloudWatch alarm on bridge_run_failures uses period 3600 and threshold 1 to page on the second failure within an hour, filtering transient blips while catching sustained outages like an expired token.
